title: Geometry - Lesson 6 Assessment: Angle Pair Relationships
description: Show mastery of complementary, supplementary, vertical, and adjacent angle relationships.

questions.question: Which equation represents two complementary angles with measures x and 64 degrees?
Find the complement of a 17-degree angle. Enter just the number.
Find the supplement of a 139-degree angle. Enter just the number.
Adjacent angles must share a vertex and one side.
questions.explanation: Sharing a vertex and a side is part of the definition of adjacent angles.

questions.question: Two lines intersect. One angle is 58 degrees. What is the measure of the vertical angle opposite it?
questions.explanation: Vertical angles are equal, so the opposite angle is 58 degrees.

questions.question: Two adjacent angles form a straight line. One angle is 82 degrees. Find the other angle. Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: A straight line measures 180 degrees, and 180 - 82 = 98.

questions.question: Which pair of angle measures is supplementary?
Two intersecting lines form an angle of 121 degrees. Find the measure of an adjacent angle. Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: Adjacent angles formed by intersecting lines make a straight angle, so 180 - 121 = 59.

questions.question: Explain the difference between vertical angles and adjacent angles.
questions.correctAnswer: Vertical angles are opposite angles formed by intersecting lines and have equal measures. Adjacent angles are next to each other and share a vertex and a side without overlapping.
questions.explanation: A complete answer should compare position and relationship: opposite and equal for vertical angles, side-by-side and sharing a side for adjacent angles.

questions.question: A missing angle x is adjacent to a 146-degree angle on a straight line. Write the equation and solve for x.
questions.explanation: The angles are supplementary because they form a straight line. Subtract 146 from 180 to get 34.
